review_scope: Full 88-line concept article read; includes, product variables and three feature conditionals remain unresolved. Marketing benefits are descriptive assertions, not measured outcomes. No complete artifact accounting, enforcement or adoption certificate.

claims.statement: Push protection is described as pre-push credential detection and blocking, distinct from retrospective leak alerts.
The article lists command-line pushes as a protected ingress path.
The article lists web UI commits as a protected ingress path.
The article lists repository file uploads as a protected ingress path.
The article lists REST API requests as a protected ingress path; this requires separate actual endpoint behavior evidence.
The listed GitHub MCP interaction coverage is expressly limited to public repositories.
The documented blocked-push path includes an explanatory message and review, sensitive-value removal and retry; it does not authorize exposing real secrets in a test.
Repository push protection can be configured at repository, organization or enterprise scope in the source model.
Repository push protection requires the product's Secret Protection enabled; the product variable remains unresolved.
Repository push protection is documented as disabled by default, unlike user push protection.
The article lists repository administrators, organization owners, security managers and enterprise owners as enablement actors; eligibility is not target-specific permission proof.
Repository protection targets the specific protected repositories rather than every repository an actor may use.
Repository push-protection bypasses generate alerts at repository, organization and enterprise security views in the source description.
The article describes an organization secret-risk report independently of push-protection enablement; report availability or counts are not enforcement evidence.
User push protection is account-specific and described as available only on the cloud website.
User push protection is documented as enabled by default.
User push protection is described as stopping secret pushes to public repositories; it is not a private-repository coverage assertion.
User-protection bypass does not generate alerts unless repository push protection is also enabled.
By default, repository writers can bypass repository push protection with a reason in the article; enablement alone therefore does not establish non-bypassability.
Under the unresolved organization/enterprise exemptions feature branch, delegated actors may both bypass and approve others' bypass requests.
Under that feature branch, exempt actors may push without triggering protection; exemption is distinct from reviewed bypass.
The alternative feature branch describes a designated group overseeing bypass requests; it must not be flattened into the exemptions branch.
The article asserts preventive security through scanning at push time and prevention before repository history; this is not measured prevention evidence.
The article asserts immediate developer feedback and faster remediation; no observed latency or remediation result is provided by this claim.
The article asserts reduced accidental credential leakage and secret sprawl; it does not quantify or verify reduction for an owned target.
The article asserts more efficient and less time-consuming secret management; it is not a measured productivity outcome.
The benefit discussion preserves user bypass, delegated repository bypass and feature-conditioned exemption scope; its security assurance language does not prove absence of exposure.
Custom-pattern detection is described for repositories in organizations; the marketing assertion does not establish recall or blocking of every non-standard secret.
Custom pattern definitions are a documented customization option after repository protection enablement.
Bypass approvers and bypass-capable actors are configurable, with full exemption dependent on a separate feature condition.
Configuring included secret patterns at organization or enterprise scope is conditional on the push-protected-pattern-configuration feature, not universally asserted.
